W3 (cost lens), after E030.

**Tip (E027).** The E026 recipe at 8.75 true epochs: 219 steps at batch 2000, with the 20/24/28/32 px phases at 15/25/30/30% of steps. It measured 5.878 s at 0.7547 on seeds 0–2. E029 and E030 share the tip's RNG stream and measured 0.7526 and 0.7492. Those two changes may have hurt, but together with E027's held-out evidence they put the population mean near 0.752–0.753. The tip sits on the bar, so any time cut first needs real accuracy.

**Time budget.** Time ≈ F + V × (pixel-weighted steps), with F ≈ 0.5 s.
- One step costs about 0.032 s at 32 px, 0.021 s at 24 px and 0.016 s at 20 px.
- Cutting 0.25 epoch saves about 0.14 s.
- Schedule-only changes (LR, LS, alpha, Lookahead interval) cost about 0 s: E029 and E030 each came in about 0.02 s faster.
- Structural savings, such as removing high-res work or backward work, come in at 1.5–4× my modelled value (E026, E028). I now scale modelled savings by about 1.5 and shade forecasts low. My last 2 time forecasts hit after this correction.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: about 1.5–2.5 s/pp.
- Early low-res phase: about 1+ s/pp (noisy).
- FreezeOut (E028): −0.52 s for about −0.2 to −0.3 pp, so about 2 s/pp. That is the best rate measured, but it still needs margin.
- No lever has a demonstrated rate above about 2 s/pp. The binding constraint is margin, not efficiency.

**Accuracy boosters are flat or negative (every result is noise or a loss):**
- LS: E013.
- Muon lr: E014.
- wd: E016, E022.
- Final LR: E009.
- Alpha exponent: E025 (−).
- Warm-up: E029 (−0.2 pp).
- Lookahead interval: E030 (−0.55 pp on the same stream, the largest drop).

The airbench averaging and LR schedule sit at a sharp local optimum: moving any part of it hurts. Prior for an untested schedule knob: −0.1 ± 0.25 pp.

**Mechanisms I believe:**
1. Lookahead endpoint averaging is worth about 1 pp (E005). It is tuned: a harder pull (E025) and sparser resets (E030) both hurt.
2. Muon is worth about +0.66 pp (E006). Filters are renormalized, so filter wd is inert.
3. Accuracy is built in the 28/32 px phases (E011, E018, E024). The earliest phase is cheap to degrade (E026), but not free.
4. Last-group width matters (E010).
5. RNG stream × seed effects move the 3-seed mean by about ±0.3 pp.

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp. The 10-seed held-out SE is about 0.1 pp.
- Time noise is about 1%.
- Any change to step count or data order re-rolls seeds 0–2.

**Unsure:**
- Loss-based dropping (I044): it is probably a uniform cut with extra gradient noise. Removing easy examples under LS 0.3 skews the loss toward noisy or mislabeled samples.
- Per-resolution whitening (I051): eigenvector sign and order are arbitrary. Unaligned bases jolt group 1 at every switch, so the net effect is likely ≤ 0.
- Whether the margin transfers to the PCIe judge.
- Whether any time-neutral booster exists. If none does, the only route is to combine FreezeOut-type savings with a more accurate (wider or longer) 32 px tail and re-balance the time.

forecasts.reason: It removes about 9% of steps on the 225-step E023 base, saving about 0.4 s, but loses about 0.3 pp, like a uniform cut. Hard-example bias under LS 0.3 adds no gain, and the rate is no better than about 1.5 s/pp.
It costs no time, but endpoint schedule tweaks have been flat or negative (E013, E025, E029, E030). Removing LS late may sharpen logits against the averaging.
About 33 steps move from 24 to 20 px. That saves about 0.17 s after my 1.5× correction, enough for the 2.5% time bar. The expected loss of about 0.2 pp straddles the 0.15 pp limit.
It adds about 3 eigh/unfold passes in prepare. Unaligned eigenbases jolt group 1 at every resolution switch, so there is no plausible gain.

cruxes: Does any lever buy accuracy for time at better than about 2 s/pp? An example would be a wider last group or a longer 32 px tail funded by FreezeOut savings. Without one, the tip cannot get faster at the bar.
What is the tip's held-out (seeds 3–22) mean? If it is ≥0.7535 there is room for I050-type trims. If it is ≤0.752, the next run must buy accuracy first.
Is the early 20 px phase really near-free (I050)? A loss of ≤0.15 pp for about 0.17 s would be the best exchange rate measured so far.
